1. Background

https://bit.ly/chapter14teachers

1. Background 1/3
AI literacy is crucial for future teachers
 For future teachers, AI literacy is crucial as it equips them with the skills and knowledge
 needed to prepare students for a world where AI is increasingly integral (Farazouli et al.,
 2024).
 Teachers with a strong understanding of AI can better integrate these technologies into
 their curricula, enhancing learning experiences and fostering critical thinking skills in
 students (Du et al., 2024).
 AI-literate teachers can cultivate a more informed and technologically adept generation,
 capable of thriving in an AI-driven landscape.
 Therefore, it is essential to prepare future teachers with sufficient knowledge and skills
 associated with AI literacy (Zhao et al., 2022).

1. Background 2/3
Effective teaching strategies for AI literacy are vital in
teacher education programs.
These strategies should encompass hands-on learning, interdisciplinary approaches,
and real-world applications of AI concepts (Han et al., 2024).
By incorporating practical experiences educators can demystify AI and make it more
accessible (Ding et al., 2024; Romero et al., 2024).
Integrating ethical discussions and societal implications of AI into the curriculum helps
future teachers understand the broader context of AI technologies (Celik et al., 2022).
Such comprehensive teaching strategies ensure that teachers are not only
knowledgeable about AI, but also able to communicate this knowledge to their students
in a meaningful and engaging way (Celik, 2023).

1. Background 3/3
We have to develop strategies to educate the next
generation of teachers in AI-enriched environment
 Despite the growing recognition of the importance of AI literacy, less is known about
 the most effective methods to foster this competence among teachers. Current
 educational programs often lack a standardized approach to integrating AI literacy,
 leading to inconsistencies in knowledge and preparedness among educators (Zhang &
 Zhang, 2024).
 Additionally, more research is needed regarding the best practices for teaching AI
 concepts, particularly in a way that is both accessible and impactful for teachers with
 diverse backgrounds (Celik, 2023)

1.1. Tool

https://bit.ly/chapter14teachers

1.1. Tool: GenAI Teachable Machine
 it is essential to understand the basic concepts of machine
learning (ML) to foster AI literacy.
  ML is a core component of AI literacy because it is one of the most widely applied
 techniques in AI (Du et al., 2024)
 To promote AI literacy among pre-service teachers, we used GenAI Teachable Machine, an
 interactive tool for K-12 learners that enables the complete supervised ML application
 workflow without coding (Pope et al., 2024).
 This tool provides a hands-on learning experience, allowing pre-service teachers to
 experiment with AI models and understand the underlying mechanisms between
 algorithms and data.
 This experiential learning process helps to understand complex AI concepts and makes
 them more tangible (Zhan & Zhang, 2024).

Ai Workshop design
The instruction carried out in the AI workshop was based on the learning
materials developed in the Generation AI project for Finnish elementary
school students and teachers (Kahila et. al, 2024).

First half of the workshop: Basic concepts and mechanisms of AI
   The first half of the workshop focused on the basic concepts of AI, its applications, and its
   impacts on everyday life.
Second half of the workshop: Data driven design
   The focus of the second half of the workshop was on co-designing and creating applications
   based on the idea selected in groups.
Machine-learning driven apps done by students: Outcome of the
workshop
   As part of the workshop, the participants of this study created 57 different apps. Examples
   included identifying recycled materials, recognizing mushrooms, classifying farm animals,

2. Methods

https://bit.ly/chapter14teachers

2. Methods
 We collected reflections from pre-service teachers through mandatory portfolios. In
 total, 106 portfolios have been submitted to date with relevant reflections .

 Participants’ portfolio reflections covered three AI related themes:
 1) the description of him/her as AI user,
 2) the use of GenAI TM in the teacher’s work,
 3) general views on the AI workshop.

 We carried out a basic qualitative analysis of the portfolio reflections using Word and
 Excel, categorising the responses into themes with sub-categories (e.g. positive and
 negative views of the workshop). Then we calculated percentages and extracted
 representative quotes.

3. Results

https://bit.ly/chapter14teachers

3. Results
Theme 1. Participants’ own view as an AI user
   Only 27% of the students had prior experience using AI tools, like ChatGPT before the course.
   After the workshop 56% of the students reported a deeper understanding of AI
Theme 2. Use of GenAI TM in the teacher’s work
   About 42% of the students' expressed the idea on how the teaching machine could be integrated with the content
   of subjects taught at school. The topics of the students' application ideas included biology (21), environmental
   studies in general (8), mathematics (6), geography (2), language teaching (3), music (2), handicrafts (1), and
   media education (1).
   Yet, 40% of the ideas dealt with teaching AI-related topics (23) or remained at the level of pedagogical planning
   without a specific idea for the application's topic (19).
   The rest of the students had no intention to use GenAI TM as a teacher or has not answered this question
Theme 3. General views on the AI workshop
   69% of the students (73) considered the AI workshop a positive learning experience and found the GenAI TM
   application easy to use.
   24% of the students didn’t respond to this theme and only 7% students provided negative opinions
